name: Juvenile Nasopharyngeal Angiofibroma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Juvenile Nasopharyngeal Angiofibroma

criteria.description: Presence of a highly vascularized mass in the nasopharynx on endoscopic examination
Characteristic findings on CT or MRI showing a vascular tumor with bone remodeling and extension into adjacent structures
Typical clinical presentation including recurrent unilateral epistaxis and nasal obstruction in adolescent males
Angiographic evidence of a hypervascular tumor supplied mainly by branches of the external carotid artery

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a vascular nasopharyngeal mass with typical clinical presentation and characteristic imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Biopsy is generally avoided due to risk of severe bleeding.

searchTerms: benign tumor in nasal area of young males

laboratory: Anemia due to chronic blood loss
imaging: CT scan showing a highly vascular nasopharyngeal mass with bone erosion
MRI demonstrating tumor extent and vascularity
Angiography revealing tumor blood supply from external carotid artery branches
other: Endoscopic visualization of a reddish, vascular mass in the nasopharynx
Histopathology showing fibrous stroma with numerous blood vessels (biopsy usually avoided)

distinguishingFeatures: Usually cutaneous or subcutaneous rather than nasopharyngeal
Benign epithelial tumor with different histology
Less vascular and no significant epistaxis
Usually arises from lateral nasal wall

redFlags: Massive recurrent epistaxis causing hemodynamic instability
Rapid tumor growth with cranial nerve deficits
references: Windfuhr JP, Remmert S. Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma: current concepts in diagnosis and treatment. Eur Arch Otorhinolaryngol. 2004.
Radkowski D, McGill T, Healy GB, et al. Angiofibroma: changes in staging and treatment. Arch Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg. 1996.
